reconstructed_theorem_text: Let I be finite, Omega a measurable space with finite measure mu, K a compact subset of R^I, and f:R^I->R twice continuously Frechet differentiable at every point of K. Fix T>0 and X:[0,infinity) x Omega -> K, where each time slice X(t,.) is measurable and, for mu-almost every omega, t->X(t,omega) is continuous on [0,T]. Let Q:I->(Omega->R). Write t_i^n=i*T/2^n, i=0,...,2^n. Assume for every coordinate j in I that sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1}(X_j(t_{i+1}^n)-X_j(t_i^n))^2 converges in mu-measure to Q_j as n tends to infinity. Define R_f(x,v)=f(x+v)-f(x)-Df(x)[v]-(1/2)*D(Df)(x)[v][v]. Then sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} R_f(X(t_i^n),X(t_{i+1}^n)-X(t_i^n)) converges in mu-measure to the identically zero random variable. The compact-valued process is coerced to R^I in this formula; the summands are signed Taylor remainders, without absolute values.
objects: Finite coordinate type I, finite measure space Omega, compact K, scalar f, T, K-valued process X, coordinate limits Q, dyadic grid, Taylor remainder R_f.
domains: X defined for all NNReal times; f on EuclideanSpace R I; Q_j arbitrary real functions on Omega; K has induced measurable/topological structure.
quantifiers: For every I,Omega,mu,K,f,T,X,Q with the stated assumptions, coordinatewise convergence for every j implies one scalar convergence of the sum of remainders.
assumptions: K compact; f is ContDiffAt R 2 at each x in K; T>0; each X(t) measurable; almost every path continuous on [0,T]; coordinate quadratic sums tend to Q_j in mu-measure.
conclusion: The dyadic sum of second-order Taylor remainders tends in mu-measure to zero.
scopes: Finite fixed horizon [0,T]; n->infinity through natural numbers; convergence in measure, not stated almost surely or in Lp. X is K-valued pointwise, while continuity holds on one full-measure path event.
constant_dependencies: No estimate or existential bound is asserted. Q may depend on j and omega. The limit conclusion is zero independent of the values of Q.
